subject: Next steps: demo pairing + dedicated capacity sizing call
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Agarwal <samir@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Aug 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — follow-up and proposal for next meeting

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the discovery earlier — great to hear how Blue Harbor is using extracted transaction metadata to power real-time risk scoring. Quick recap of what I heard:
- ~250k monthly transactions, peak bursts up to 2k TPS for short windows, average inference per transaction ~180 tokens (prompt+response).
- Primary SLAs: p99 latency target of ~450ms for single-call risk checks; higher-throughput batch scoring for nightly reconciliation is OK.
- Data controls: VPC private deployment preferred; SOC2 attestation required.

To move forward, I suggest two items:
1) A 45-minute demo + ops walkthrough where we show the integration points and mock requests.
2) A dedicated capacity sizing call (30–45 mins) with our infra team to validate throughput assumptions, concurrency, and KV-cache recommendations.

Are you available next week for the sizing call? Here are a few slots that work for our infra engineers (Karthik and Evelyn are cc'd):
- Tue 8/29, 10:00–10:45 PT
- Wed 8/30, 14:00–14:45 PT
- Thu 8/31, 09:00–09:45 PT

If none of these work, send a couple of times and we’ll align. I’ve attached a short Redwood Sizing Checklist to help you surface any perf numbers ahead of the call.

Next steps we typically take before the sizing session:
- Share a sample load profile (CSV) — ideal: 7 days including peak windows.
- Provide representative prompts and typical response sizes.
- Confirm data retention and regional constraints.

Thanks — looking forward to locking a slot.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Attachment: Redwood_Sizing_Checklist.pdf (1 page)
From: Samir Agarwal <samir@blueharbor.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Aug 2028 18:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — follow-up and proposal for next meeting

Laura — thanks for the clear recap. That matches our internal read. Happy to move forward.

We can do Tue 8/29 at 10am PT. I’ll be joined by our lead infra engineer (Maya Singh) and our product manager (Carlos Ruiz). A couple of quick details from our side so the sizing call is productive:
- Typical steady-state TPS: 90–120 TPS.
- Peak flash windows: up to ~1.8k TPS for ~10–12 minutes during batch ingestion events.
- Average tokens per inference: 170–200 tokens (most responses are short).
- We currently batch inbound events in 50–200 item windows for offline scoring; realtime path is single-request synchronous.

I’ll upload a 72-hr sample request trace to the Drive link you shared and attach a sanitized CSV (blueharbor_sample_load_profile.csv).

Also: SOC2 is a must. Can you confirm who from Redwood’s compliance team we can speak to or whether that gets covered during the private deployment onboarding?

See you Tue.

—Samir
Samir Agarwal
Head of Engineering | Blue Harbor Payments
samir@blueharbor.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Agarwal <samir@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — follow-up and proposal for next meeting

Perfect — I’ve booked Tue 8/29 10:00–10:45 PT on our side and sent a calendar invite. Karthik and Evelyn will lead the sizing conversation; Karthik will walk throughput/queueing assumptions and Evelyn will cover p99 latency ops and caching.

On SOC2: our compliance lead (Maria Gomez) typically joins the onboarding calls for Private deployments and can provide our SOC2 report and evidence matrix. Maria isn’t needed for the sizing call, but I can introduce you on the kickoff if that’s helpful.

Prep checklist for Tuesday (small asks so the session is focused):
- Drive link with sample trace (thanks, Samir)
- A single representative prompt and a short set of failing vs. acceptable latency examples
- Any network egress or regional constraints (which cloud regions you prefer)

I’ve attached the Redwood_Sizing_Checklist again and included a short internal note for the team.

If you want us to also demonstrate a quick mock integration during the same slot, say so and we’ll add 15 minutes to the invite.

Thanks — invite is on the way.

Best,
Laura
